text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the pattern of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest in your left great toe, hips, and knees, is the pain also accompanied by morning stiffness that typically lasts less than 30 minutes?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis

The clinical picture of pain localized to the great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest is highly characteristic of osteoarthritis. The lack of prolonged morning stiffness further supports this diagnosis over inflammatory arthropathies.
